deltas.behavior_text: the nova-face-noticed rule is installed only when NOVA_FACE_HOLD is off and tombstoned only when it is on (t12 first installed then retired it on every boot: two overlay writes and two reloads per start); commit 8827b56

Nova's own opening utterance at every Sonic session start counts as conversation activity, so the gaze stack turns toward the last sound and tries the face lock at every boot (observed 09:31:17 BST); by design of c7 (Nova speaking is conversation), noted as a wart to revisit

an unconfirmed release_face (ok:null or ok:false) still clears the gaze stack's lock_held without marking LockState, so a stale 'held' belief cannot suppress later attempts while LockState keeps its only-ok:true rule (t9 decision)
browser progress cues for 'Navigating to ...' and 'Starting a cloud browser session...' are log lines only, not injects: the two narrated phases are start and working (t2 decision)
an out-of-process 'reachy_nova.harness status' reports eyes: unknown by design (the belief lives in the harness process); the live journal carries the no-frames/restored lines

the runtime's face-lost notices reach Sonic every 20-40 s while a lock is held on a moving person (seven 'motion/face-lost' injects in three minutes, 10:50:33-10:53:26) — noisy with the 6.7 Hz tick and 0.5 s detection cadence; and the gaze stack re-submits lock_face ('already locked', ok:true) after an engine-heartbeat flap under that load

the runtime's own lock-release event reaches the gaze stack with reason=None ('runtime dropped the lock reason=None') although the runtime published reason=requested — the bus tap reads the reason from the wrong level of the event payload; cosmetic, the belief still clears

under a 1.0 s detection interval the runtime's face box (1.5 s TTL) blanks on a single missed detection: motion/face-lost fired twice (absent_s=3.0) in a 30 s hold with the person present; the TTL should track the interval (runtime side, reachy-mini-cli #181/#180)

the head settles about a third of the way to the face and chases it one detection cycle at a time: the runtime's face-lock aim is open-loop (absolute target = box offset x 20 deg against an 87 deg camera FOV), filed as reachy-mini-cli #181; Ori: 'It follows me in a delay', 'not focusing on me on center of the camera'

the overlay validator accepts the runtime's names table (at most 8 letters-only names of 3+ characters) and a name_mentioned predicate; the names write itself is deferred until reachy-mini-cli #177 is on the device, because the current runtime refuses the whole file

the harness keeps the runtime's feel-alive base layer alive: whenever the runtime's active list lacks it and nothing inhibits it, one bounded passive run_behavior feel-alive (300 s) is re-issued, in every layer, never under a held auto lock, reset by every release — a workaround for reachy-mini-cli #183
